title: Corvus
name: corvus
description: Self-hosted web gateway: a reverse proxy as easy as Nginx Proxy Manager, with free Let's Encrypt certificates, attack blocking (WAF rules, automatic bans, rate limits, browser challenge), a live traffic monitor, alerts and a waiting room for traffic spikes. One container. Source: https://github.com/corvus-gateway/corvus

env.name: CORVUS_SETUP_TOKEN
env.label: Setup token (optional)
env.description: One-time token for creating the administrator, at least 12 characters. Leave empty to use a random token printed in the container log.

note: Corvus needs ports 80 and 443 on the host for your sites and Let's Encrypt, and serves its admin console on 9443 (HTTPS, self-signed certificate at first; keep this port off the internet). Open https://<your-host>:9443, enter the setup token (the one you set, or the setup_token line in the container log) and create the administrator. Only someone with the token can do this. All data, certificates and keys are stored in the /data volume; back it up. Docs: corvusgateway.org
